rashi.eng: *and… wall.* the building of a wall of bricks.

rashi.heb:
*ואף שמהתהום.* 
ואף שמותם של בונים ראשי הבנין שאלנו להם כדי להודיעך:
rashi.eng: *also… their names.* We also asked them the names of the builders, the heads of the construction, in order to let you know.

rashi.heb:
*די נכתוב.* 
אשר נכתוב שמות האנשים אליך:
rashi.eng: *that we should write.* that we should write to you the names of the men.

rashi.heb:
*די בראשיהם.* 
אשר בעצמם וברשותם קמו לבנות הבית:
rashi.eng: *who are at their head.* in whose counsel and authorization they arose to build the House.

notes.174: (sn): This great king of Israel would, of course, be Solomon.

rashi.heb:
*וכנמא פתגמא.* 
כמו שנאמר הדבר:
rashi.eng: *And as follows.* Aram. וּכְנֵמָא, as we shall state the matter.

rashi.heb:
*התיבונא.* 
השיבו לנו דבר:
rashi.eng: *they gave us a reply.* They answered us a word.

rashi.heb:
*אנחנא המו.* 
אנחנו הם עבדיו של אלהי השמים והארץ:
rashi.eng: *We are.* We are the servants of the God of the heavens and the earth.

rashi.heb:
*ובנין ביתא.* 
ואנו בונין הבית אשר היה בנוי קודם לכן שנים רבות:
rashi.eng: *and we are building the House.* And we are building the House that was built many years ago.

rashi.heb:
*ומלך לישראל רב.* 
ומלך גדול שהיה לישראל הוא שלמה המלך בנה אותו ויסד אותו:
rashi.eng: *and a great king of Israel.* And a great king that Israel had, viz. King Solomon, built it and founded it.

notes.177: (sn): A reference to the catastrophic events of 586 b.c.

rashi.heb:
*להן.* 
ועכשיו מפני אשר הכעיסו אבותינו לאלהי השמים מסר אותם ביד מלך בבל הכשדי והבית הזה החריב ואת העם הגלה לבבל:
rashi.eng: *But now.* But now, since our forefathers angered the God of the heavens, He delivered them into the hands of the Chaldean king of Babylon, and he destroyed this House and exiled the people to Babylon.

notes.178: (sn): Cyrus was actually a Persian king, but when he conquered Babylon in 539 b.c. he apparently appropriated to himself the additional title “king of Babylon.” The Syriac Peshitta substitutes “Persia” for “Babylon” here, but this is probably a hyper-correction.

rashi.heb:
*ברם.* 
אך בשנה אחת לכורש מלך בבל צוה כורש בדבר הזה לבנות הבית:
rashi.eng: *But.* But in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, Cyrus issued a command to build the House.

rashi.heb:
*ואף מאניא.* 
כלי הקדש של כסף וזהב אשר הוציא נבוכדנצר מן ההיכל שבירושלים והוליכם להיכלו שבבבל הוציא אותם כורש מהיכל מלך בבל ומסרם ליד ששבצר דניאל ששמו כך:
rashi.eng: *And also the vessels.* the holy vessels of silver and gold, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the Temple that is in Jerusalem and brought to his temple that is in Babylon. Cyrus took them out of the temple of the king of Babylon and delivered them to the hand of Sheshbazzar-Daniel, who was called by that name.

rashi.heb:
*והיבל המו.* 
והוליך אותם:
rashi.eng: *and brought them.* [as translated,] and brought them.

rashi.heb:
*הנפק המו.* 
הוציא אותם:
rashi.eng: *had taken out.* [as translated,] had taken them out.

rashi.heb:
*די פחה שמה.* 
שהוא היה נשיא ופחת ונקרא שמו פחה:
rashi.eng: *whom he appointed governor.* for he was a prince and a governor and was called by the name governor.

rashi.heb:
*ואמר לה.* 
וכך אמר לו כורש לששבצר אלה הכלים קח ולך והורד אותם בהיכל אשר בירושלים וביתו של הקב"ה יהא בנוי על מקומו:
rashi.eng: *And he said to him.* And so did Cyrus say to Sheshbazzar, “Take these vessels and bring them down into the Temple that is in Jerusalem, and the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, shall be built on its place.”

rashi.heb:
*אדין.* 
אז:
rashi.eng: *then.* [as translated,] then.

rashi.heb:
*ששבצר דך.* 
זה בא ונתן כתלי ביתו של הקב"ה אשר בירושלים ומאז ועד עתה היה הבית בנוי ולא נגמר הבנין:
rashi.eng: *this Sheshbazzar.* Aram. דֵּ, came and built the walls of the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, that is in Jerusalem, and from then until now, the House has been built, but the building has not been completed.

notes.183: (tn): Aram “if upon the king it is good.”
notes.184: (tn): Aram “the house of the treasures of the king.”

rashi.heb:
*וכען.* 
ועתה אם על המלך טוב יהיה הדבר ידוע ומבוקר בבית גנזיו של מלך אשר שם בבבל:
rashi.eng: *And now.* And now, if it pleases the king, let the matter be known and searched out in the king’s archives, which is located in Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*הן איתי.* 
אם יש המעשה הזה אשר מפי כורש יצא דבר לבנות בית זה אשר בירושלים:
rashi.eng: *whether it is so.* whether this incident is so, that permission was issued by Cyrus to build this House, which is in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*ורעות מלכא.* 
רצון המלך על כן ישלח אלינו:
rashi.eng: *and the will of the king.* And the will of the king concerning this he shall send to us.

rashi.heb:
*עלינא.* 
אלינו ע"כ מכתב האגרת אשר שלחו תתני ושתר בוזני:
rashi.eng: *to us.* Aram. עֲלֶינָא, lit. on us. Until here is the text of the letter that Tattenai and Shethar- bozenai sent.

rashi.heb:
*באדין.* 
אז כאשר הגיע המכתב ליד דריוש:
rashi.eng: *Then.* then when the letter reached Darius’s hand.

rashi.heb:
*שם טעם.* 
צוה המלך הדבר:
rashi.eng: *gave an order.* The king ordered the matter.

rashi.heb:
*ובקרו.* 
ובדקו בבית הספרים שהאוצרות מונחים שם בבבל:
rashi.eng: *and they searched.* They searched in the library where the archives were stored in Babylon.

notes.186: (tc): The translation reads בִירְתָא (birta’, citadel”) rather than the reading בְּבִירְתָא (b�vireta’, “in the citadel”) found in the MT. The MT probably experienced dittography here.

rashi.heb:
*והשתכח באחמתא.* 
ונמצא מכתב של מגילה אחת שם באחמתא כן פתרו אנשי הפתרון שהוא כלי העשוי לאגרות ולגליונים ולספרים והעמידוהו מגזרת חמת מים והאל"ף אשר בתיבה אינה עיקר כיתר המלין אשר בשאר ל' ארמית:
rashi.eng: *And there was found in a pouch.* And a text of one scroll was found there in an אַחְמְתָא. So did the interpreters interpret, that it is a receptacle made for letters, written sheets and books, and they established it from the root of (Gen. 21:14): “a skin of water (וְחֵמַת מַיִם),” and the “aleph” in the word is not a radical, like the rest of the Aramaic language.

rashi.heb:
*בבירתא.* 
באותה בירה אשר במדי המדינה:
rashi.eng: *in the citadel.* in that citadel that was in the province of Media.

rashi.heb:
*וכן כתיב.* 
וכן היה כתוב בתוכה זכרון שלה:
rashi.eng: *and so was written.* and so was written therein its memorandum.

notes.187: (tn): Aram “In the first year of Cyrus the king.”
notes.188: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.189: (tn): Aram “raised”; or perhaps “retained” (so NASB; cf. NLT), referring to the original foundations of Solomon’s temple.
notes.190: (tc): The Syriac Peshitta reads “twenty cubits” here, a measurement probably derived from dimensions given elsewhere for Solomon’s temple. According to 1 Kgs 6:2 the dimensions of the Solomonic temple were as follows: length, 60 cubits; width, 20 cubits; height, 30 cubits. Since one would expect the dimensions cited in Ezra 6:3 to correspond to those of Solomon’s temple, it is odd that no dimension for length is provided. The Syriac has apparently harmonized the width dimension provided here (“twenty cubits”) to that given in 1 Kgs 6:2.
notes.191: (tn): Aram “Its height sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits.” The standard cubit in the OT is assumed by most authorities to be about eighteen inches (45 cm) long.

rashi.heb:
*בית אלהא בירושלים.* 
בבית אלהים בירושלים מה יהא עליו הבית יבנה:
rashi.eng: *the House of God in Jerusalem.* regarding the House of God in Jerusalem; what should be with it?“The House should be built.”

rashi.heb:
*אתר די דבחין.* 
שהוא מקום שזובחים שם זבח:
rashi.eng: *a place where they offer up sacrifices.* which is a place where they offer up sacrifices.

rashi.heb:
*ואושוהי מסובלין.* 
וכותליו יהיו מיוסדין, כמו ואושיא יחיטו (לעיל):
rashi.eng: *and its walls should be founded.* Aram. וְאֻשּׁוֹהִי. And its walls should be founded, like (4:12): “and its walls (וְאֻשַּׁיָא) they have joined.”

rashi.heb:
*רומיה אמין שתין.* 
רום הבית ששים אמה וששים אמה רחבו:
rashi.eng: *its height sixty cubits.* the height of the House was sixty cubits, and sixty cubits was its width.

notes.193: (tc): The translation follows the LXX reading חַד (khad, “one”) rather than the MT חֲדַת (khadat, “new”). If the MT reading “new” is understood to mean freshly cut timber that has not yet been seasoned it would seem to be an odd choice for construction material.

rashi.heb:
*נדבכין.* 
ל' כתלים וקירות הכתלים היו של אבן גלל:
rashi.eng: *rows.* Aram. נִדְבָּכִין, an expression for walls. The walls were of marble.

rashi.heb: *גלל.* מרמר"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *marble.* Aram. גְּלָל (marmre in Old French).

rashi.heb:
*ונדבך.* 
וכותל של עץ חדש מבפנים כענין בנין הבית אשר בנה שלמה:
rashi.eng: *and a row.* and a wall of new wood from within, in the manner of the building of the Temple that Solomon built.

rashi.heb:
*ונפקתא.* 
והוצאה לצורך הבית ולשאר דברים אשר לבית תנתן להם מבית המלך:
rashi.eng: *and the expenditures.* And the expenditures for the needs of the House and for the other matters pertaining to the House shall be given them from the royal palace.

rashi.heb:
*ואף מאני.* 
ואף כלי הקדש של בית האלהים של זהב וכסף אשר נבוכדנצר הוציאם מן היכל שבירושלים והוליכם לבבל:
rashi.eng: *And also the vessels of.* and also the sacred vessels of the House of God, of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the Temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*והיבל.* 
אשר הוליך:
rashi.eng: *let them be given over.* [as translated,] let them be given over.

rashi.heb:
*יהתיבון.* 
ינתנו:
rashi.eng: *and brought.* which he brought.

rashi.heb:
*ויהך.* 
ילך כל המעשה הזה להיכל אשר בירושלים למקומו:
rashi.eng: *and brought.* Let all this work be brought to the Temple that is in Jerusalem, to its place.

rashi.heb:
*ותחת.* 
ויהי מונח בביתו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *and it shall be deposited.* And it shall be deposited in the House of the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*כען תתני וגו'.* 
זו היא תשובה אשר השיב דריוש אל תתני ושתר בוזני:
rashi.eng: *Now, Tattenai.* This is the reply with which Darius answered Tattenai and Shethar-Bozenai.

rashi.heb:
*די בעבר נהרה.* 
לצד ארץ ישראל שהוא עבר הנהר לאותן שבבבל:
rashi.eng: *who are on the other side of the river.* to the side of the land of Israel, which is the other side of the river to those in Babylon

rashi.heb:
*רחיקין הוו מן תמה.* 
רחוקים תהיו משם מבנין בהמ"ק שלא תרפו ידי עושי המלאכה:
rashi.eng: *distance yourselves from there.* Distance yourselves from the building of the Temple, so that you do not disturb the workers.

notes.196: (tc): For the MT reading “the work on this temple of God” the LXX reads “the servant of the Lord Zurababel” [= Zerubbabel].

rashi.heb:
*דך.* 
זה:
rashi.eng: *this.* [as translated,] this.

rashi.heb:
*פחת יהודיא.* 
שלטוני היהודים יעשו דבר זה:
rashi.eng: *the governors of the Jews.* The rulers of the Jews shall do this thing.

rashi.heb:
*ולשבי יהודיא.* 
ולזקני היהודים אני מצוה:
rashi.eng: *and to the elders of the Jews.* And to the elders of the Jews I command.

rashi.heb:
*בית אלהא דך.* 
בית אלהים זה:
rashi.eng: *this House of God.* [as translated,] this House of God.

notes.197: (tn): The words “of the work” are not in the Aramaic, but are supplied in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ומני שים טעם.* 
וממני יהיה צווי זה:
rashi.eng: *And from me shall be issued an order.* And from me this command will go forth.

rashi.heb:
*למא די תעבדון.* 
לאותו בנין המלאכה אשר תעשון עם זקני היהודים האלה לבנות ביתו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *regarding what you shall do.* regarding that building, the work that you shall do with these elders of the Jews to build the House of the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*ומנכסי מלכא.* 
מנכסי המלך יהיו עושים הבנין הזה:
rashi.eng: *and from the king’s property.* And from the king’s property they shall make ths building.

rashi.heb:
*די מדת עבר נהרה.* 
מן המס של עבר הנהר אשר למלך:
rashi.eng: *from the taxes of the other side of the river.* from the taxes of the other side of the river, which belong to the king.

rashi.heb:
*מדת.* 
מדת מס כמו מנדה בלו והלך (לעיל ד'):
rashi.eng: *taxes.* Aram. מִדַּת, tax, like (4:13): “the king’s due (מִנְדָּה), the head tax, or the meal tax.”

rashi.heb: *אספרנא.*  מהרה יבנה הבנין אספרנה אישפלונטמנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *quickly.* Aram. אָסְפַּרְנָא. The building shall quickly be built; esploytosemant in Old French.

rashi.heb:
*נפקתא תהוא מתיהבא.* 
הוצאה תהיה ניתנת לאנשים האלה אשר לא יתבטלו ממלאכתן:
rashi.eng: *The expenses shall be given.* The expenses shall be given to these men so that they should not idle from their work.

rashi.heb:
*ומה חשחן.* 
ומה שיהיו חוששין:
rashi.eng: *And what they require.* and what they are concerned about.

rashi.heb:
*ובני תורין.* 
בני בקר ואילים וכבשים לעולות לאלהי השמים:
rashi.eng: *and young bulls.* young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven.

rashi.heb:
*וחנטין.* 
לסלתות:
rashi.eng: *wheat.* for fine flour.

rashi.heb:
*ומלח.* 
לקרבנות:
rashi.eng: *salt.* for sacrifices.

rashi.heb:
*ויין.* 
לנסכים:
rashi.eng: *wine.* for libations.

rashi.heb:
*ושמן.* 
למנחות כאשר יאמרו הכהנים אשר בירושלים יהי נתון להם דבר יום ביומו:
rashi.eng: *and oil.* for the meal-offerings. When the priests who are in Jerusalem will say [what they need], that shall be given to them the requirements of each day on its day.

rashi.heb:
*די לא שלו.* 
בלא דיחוי שנ"צ דישטורבי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *without delay.* Aram. דִּי לָא שָּׁלוּ (son destorber in Old French).

notes.199: (tn): Aram “for the life of the king and his sons.”

rashi.heb:
*די להון.* 
למען אשר יהיו מקריבים ניחוחים לאלהי השמים ויהיו מתפללים על חיי המלך ובניו:
rashi.eng: *That they should.* in order that they should offer up pleasing sacrificing to the God of the heavens, and that they should pray for the life of the king and his children.

notes.200: (sn): The practice referred to in v. 11 has been understood in various ways: hanging (cf. 1 Esd 6:32 and KJV); flogging (cf. NEB, NLT); impalement (BDB 1091 s.v. זְקַף; HALOT 1914 s.v. מחא hitpe; cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV). The latter seems the most likely.

rashi.heb:
*ומני שים טעם.* 
וממני שים צווי ושימת דבר אשר כל אדם אשר ישנה דבר זה יתנסח. יחרב עציו מביתו שיחרב ביתו, יתנסח כמו ונסחתם מעל האדמה (דברים כ״ח:ס״ג):
rashi.eng: *And an order is issued by me.* And a command is issued by me, along with the issue of a word regarding any person who disobeys this word.

rashi.heb:
*וזקיף יתמחא עלוהי.* 
ועץ לתלותו יהא גבוה עליו שיתלה על העץ:
rashi.eng: *shall be torn.* Aram. יִתְנְסַח. The beams of his house shall be destroyed. יִתְנְסַח is like (Deut. 28:63): “and you shall be uprooted (וְנִסַחְתֶּם) from the land.”

rashi.heb:
*וביתה נולו יתעבד.* 
וביתו יעשה אשפה על כך:
rashi.eng: *and a gallows upon which to place him.* And a gallows upon which to hang him shall be [raised up] high, so that he be hanged upon the gallows.

rashi.heb:
*נולו.* 
ענין טינוף ומחראות:
rashi.eng: *and his house shall be made a dungheap.* and his house shall be made a dungheap because of this. נְוָלוּ connotes filth and excrement.

rashi.heb:
*ואלהא די שכן שמיה.* 
והאלהים אשר שכן שמו שם:
rashi.eng: *And God, Who caused His name to rest there.* [as translated,] and God, Who caused His name to rest there.

rashi.heb:
*ימגר.* 
ימגר ויפגר כל אותו מלך וכל אותו עם אשר ישלח ידו להחריב ולהשחית ביתו זה של ה' אשר בירושלים:
rashi.eng: *will cast down.* will cast down and destroy any such king and any such people that will stretch forth a hand to lay waste and destroy His house that is in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*שמת טעם.* 
שמתי ציווי דבר זה אשר יעשה הבנין מהרה עד כאן תשובתו של דריוש:
rashi.eng: *have issued an edict.* I have issued a command concerning this matter, that the building be constructed swiftly. Until here is Darius’s reply.

rashi.heb:
*כנמא.* 
כאשר נאמר:
rashi.eng: *as was said.* [as translated,] as was said.

rashi.heb:
*אספרנא עבדו.* 
מהרה עשו:
rashi.eng: *acted swiftly.* [as translated,] acted swiftly.

notes.207: (tn): Aram “in” or “by,” in the sense of accompaniment.

rashi.heb:
*ושבי יהודיא.* 
וזקני היהודים היו בונין ומצליחין במלאכתן כנבואת חגי וזכריה ובנו ויסדו את הבנין מן צווי של אלהי ישראל ומרשות כורש מלך פרס הראשון אשר הוחל יסוד הבנין בימיו ומרשות דריוש זה מלך פרס:
rashi.eng: *And the elders of the Jews.* And the elders of the Jews were building and succeeding in their work, according to the prophecy of Haggai and Zechariah, and they built and founded the building by the command of the God of Israel and by the authorization of Cyrus, the first king of Persia, in whose days the laying of the foundation was commenced, and by the authorization of this Darius, the king of Persia.

rashi.heb:
*וארתחששתא.* 
הוא דריוש ונקרא ארתחששתא ע"ש המדינה והמלכות כי כל מלכי פרס היו נקראים כך כאשר כל מלכי מצרים נקראים פרעה:
rashi.eng: *and Artaxerxes.* He is Darius, but he was called Artaxerxes because of the province and the kingdom, for all kings of Persia were thus named just as all the kings of Egypt were called Pharaoh.

notes.208: (sn): The sixth year of the reign of Darius would be ca. 516 B.C.

rashi.heb:
*ושיציא.* 
ביתה דנה וסוף תשלום בית זה היה עד יום שלישי לחדש אדר שהיא שנת שש לדריוש המלך ונמצא בנין הבית היה ד' שנים:
rashi.eng: *And the completion of this House.* And the end of the completion of this House was until the third day of the month of Adar, which is the sixth year of King Darius; hence the building of the House took four years.

rashi.heb:
*והקריבו לחנוכת.* 
הקריבו לחנוכת בית זה קרבנות הללו והוראת שעה היתה:
rashi.eng: *And they offered up for the dedication.* They offered up for the dedication of this House these sacrifices, and it was a temporary ruling.

notes.211: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*והקימו כהניא בפלוגתהון.* 
שהיו הכהנים חלוקים בעבודתם ולוי' במשמרות':
rashi.eng: *Now they set up the priests in their divisions.* for the priests were divided in their service and the Levites in their watches.

notes.213: (sn): At this point the language of the book reverts from Aramaic (4:8–6:18) back to Hebrew. Aramaic will again be used in Ezra 7:12-26.
notes.214: (tn, Heb): “the sons of the exile.” So also in v. 20.

rashi.heb:
*את הפסח.* 
עכשיו עשו ישראל את הפסח בי"ד בניסן זה הבא אחר אדר זה שהושלם הבנין בו:
rashi.eng: *the Passover [offering].* Now Israel made the Passover offering on this fourteenth of Nissan, which followed this Adar, when the building was completed.

notes.215: (tn, Heb): “as one.” The expression is best understood as referring to the unity shown by the religious leaders in preparing themselves for the observance of Passover. On the meaning of the Hebrew phrase see DCH 1:182 s.v. אֶחָד 3b. See also HALOT 30 s.v. אֶחָד 5.

rashi.heb:
*ולהם.* 
ולעצמם:
rashi.eng: *and for themselves.* Heb. וְלָהֶם, lit. and for them, and for themselves.

notes.217: (tn, Heb): “who had separated from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to them.”

rashi.heb:
*וכל הנבדל.* 
הם הגרים שנבדלו מטומאת העבוד' כוכבים לידבק בישראל:
rashi.eng: *and whoever separated.* They are the proselytes, who were separated from the defilement of the nations to cleave to Israel.

notes.219: (sn): The expression “king of Assyria” is anachronistic, since Assyria fell in 612 b.c., long before the events of this chapter. Perhaps the expression is intended subtly to contrast earlier kings of Assyria who were hostile toward Israel with this Persian king who showed them favor.

rashi.heb:
*והסב לב מלך אשור עליהם.* 
והקב"ה הסב לב מלך אשור על ישראל היושבים בממשלתו בארץ אשור להחזיקם ולסייע במלאכת הבנין:
rashi.eng: *and turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them.* And the Holy One, blessed be He, turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward the Israelites who were dwelling under his dominion in the land of Assyria, to strengthen them and to assist in the work of the building.

notes.221: (sn): If the Artaxerxes of Ezra 7:1 is Artaxerxes I Longimanus (ca. 464–423 B.C.), Ezra must have arrived in Jerusalem ca. 458 B.C., since Ezra 7:7-8 connects the time of his arrival to the seventh year of the king. The arrival of Nehemiah is then linked to the twentieth year of the king (Neh 1:1), or ca. 445 B.C. Some scholars, however, have suggested that Ezra 7:7 should be read as “the thirty-seventh year” rather than “the seventh year.” This would have Ezra coming to Jerusalem after, rather than before, the arrival of Nehemiah. Others have taken the seventh year of Ezra 7:7-8 to refer not to Artaxerxes I but to Artaxerxes II, who ruled ca. 404–358 B.C. In this understanding Ezra would have returned to Jerusalem ca. 398 B.C., a good many years after the return of Nehemiah. Neither of these views is certain, however, and it seems better to retain the traditional understanding of the chronological sequence of returns by Ezra and Nehemiah. With this understanding there is a gap of about fifty-eight years between chapter six, which describes the dedication of the temple in 516 b.c., and chapter seven, which opens with Ezra’s coming to Jerusalem in 458 b.c.
notes.222: (tn): The words “came up from Babylon” do not appear in the Hebrew text until v. 6. They have been supplied here for the sake of clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ואחר הדברים האלה.* 
של בנין הבית:
rashi.eng: *And after these incidents.* of the building of the House.

rashi.heb:
*ארתחשסתא.* 
הוא דריוש:
rashi.eng: *Artaxerxes.* That is Darius.

rashi.heb:
*ויתן לו המלך.* 
דריוש:
rashi.eng: *and the king granted him.* [i.e., King] Darius.

rashi.heb:
*כיד ה' אלהיו עליו.* 
כאשר צוה הקב"ה עליו ומקרא מסורס הוא ויתן לו המלך כל בקשתו כיד ה' אלהיו עליו ואמרו רז"ל עזרא הוא מלאכי:
rashi.eng: *according to the command of the Lord his God upon him.* as the Holy One, blessed be He, had commanded him. This verse is transposed [its meaning being]: and the King granted him his entire request, according to the command of the Lord upon him. And our Rabbis said (Meg. 15a) that Ezra and Malachi were one and the same.

notes.223: (tc, Heb): The translation reads the Hiphil singular וַיַּעֲל (vayya’al, “he [Ezra] brought up”) rather than the Qal plural וַיַּעַלוּ (vayya’alu, “they came up”) of the MT. “he brought”; the referent (Ezra) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.224: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*בשנת שבע.* 
היא שנה אחר תשלום הבית:
rashi.eng: *in the seventh year.* That is a year after the completion of the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*לאתחשסתא.* 
הוא דריוש:
rashi.eng: *of Artaxerxes.* That is Darius.

rashi.heb:
*בחדש החמישי.* 
הוא חדש אב כי באחד לחודש ניסן אותו היום היתה תחלת עלייתם מבבל ובאחד לחדש אב באו לירושלים:
rashi.eng: *in the fifth month.* i.e., the month of Av, for the first of the month of Nissan was the beginning of their ascent from Babylon, and on the first of the month of Av they arrived in Jerusalem.

notes.225: (tc): The translation reads יִסַּד (yissad, “he appointed” [= determined]) rather than the reading יְסֻד (y�sud, “foundation”) of the MT. (The words “to make” are supplied in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.)
notes.226: (sn): Apparently it took the caravan almost four months to make the five hundred mile journey.

rashi.heb:
*יסוד המעלה.* 
יסוד תחלת העליה:
rashi.eng: *was the commencement of the ascent.* the foundation of the commencement of the ascent.

rashi.heb:
*כיד אלהיו.* 
כאשר הצליחו יד הקב"ה שהיתה ידו טובה עליו להצליחו בדרכיו:
rashi.eng: *according to the… hand of his God.* as the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, caused him to succeed, for His hand was good upon him to make him succeed in his way.

notes.228: (tn, Heb): “to do and to teach.” The expression may be a hendiadys, in which case it would have the sense of “effectively teaching.”

rashi.heb:
*כי עזרא וגו'.* 
ועל כן הלך והצליח בדרכו שהרי עזרא הכין לבבו וגומר נותן טעם לדבריו:
rashi.eng: *For Ezra….* Therefore, he went and prospered in his way, because Ezra prepared his heart, etc. He gives a reason for his words.

notes.230: (tn, Heb): “the priest, the scribe.” So also in v. 21.
notes.231: (tn): The words “Ezra was” are not in the Hebrew text but have been added in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וזה פרשגן הנשתוון.* 
וזה פתשגן הכתב:
rashi.eng: *And this is the interpretation of the writ.* Heb. הַכְּתָב פַתְשֶּׁגֶן.

rashi.heb:
*וחקיו על ישראל.* 
ואת חקיו אשר צוה על ישראל לשמרם:
rashi.eng: *and His statutes to Israel.* and His statutes that He commanded Israel to keep.

notes.232: (sn): Ezra 7:12-26 is written in Aramaic rather than Hebrew.

rashi.heb:
*ספר דתא.* 
ספר תורה:
rashi.eng: *who has mastered… and Ke’eneth.* He has mastered it in his hand.

rashi.heb:
*גמיר וכענת.* 
ספיקא היא בידו:
rashi.eng: *the Book of Law.* [as translated,] the Book of Law.

notes.233: (tn, Heb): “from me is placed a decree.” So also in v. 21.
notes.234: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*מני שים טעם.* 
ממני יוצא הרשות כי כל אשר נדבה רוחו אותו מן ישראל מן הכהנים והלוים ללכת לירושלים ילכו עמך:
rashi.eng: *An order is issued by me.* The authorization emanates from me that whoever of Israel, of the priests, or of the Levites, whose heart prompts him to go to Jerusalem, may go with you.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל.* 
בשביל כך מאת המלך ושבעת יועציו רואי פני המלך אתה שלוח:
rashi.eng: *Because of this.* Because of this, you are sent from the king and his seven advisors who saw the king’s face.

rashi.heb:
*ושבעת יעטוהי.* 
ושבע יועציו הם שבעה רואי פני המלך:
rashi.eng: *and his seven advisors.* and his seven advisors; they are the seven who see the king’s face.

rashi.heb:
*לבקרה על יהוד.* 
כדי לדרוש ולבדוק על היהודים אשר בירושלים אם הם עסוקים בתורתו של הקב"ה אשר בידך:
rashi.eng: *to search out Judea.* An order to seek and to search out the Jews who are in Jerusalem, to see whether they are engaged in the Torah of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is in your hand.

rashi.heb:
*ולהיבלה.* 
ולהוליך כסף וזהב של המלך ויועציו אשר התנדב לאלהי ישראל לתקן ביתו אשר משכנו וביתו בירושלים:
rashi.eng: *And to bring.* and to bring the silver and gold of the king and his advisors that they donated to the God of Israel, to maintain His House, Whose habitation and House are in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*וכל כסף ודהב.* 
וכל נדבת כסף וזהב אשר תמצא במדינת בבל עם שאר נדבת העם והכהנים אשר מתנדבים לביתו של הקב"ה אשר בירושלים תוליך הכל לירושלים:
rashi.eng: *And all the silver and gold.* and all the silver and gold that you will find in the province of Babylon, together with the donations of the people and the priests that they will donate to the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is in Jerusalem; you shall take everything to Jerusalem.

notes.238: (tn): Aram “their meal offerings and their libations.”

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל דנה.* 
ובשביל כך של עבודות המקדש מהרה תקנה בכסף זה בקר ואילים וכבשים וזבחים ומנחות ונסכי' ותקריבם על המזבח של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *Because of this.* And because of this, because it is for the service of the Sanctuary, you shall quickly purchase with this money cattle, rams and lambs; sacrifices, meal-offerings, and libations, and you shall offer them up on the altar of the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*ומה די עלך.* 
ואשר ייטיב לך ולאחיך במותר הכסף והזהב לעשות כרצונו של הקב"ה תעשו:
rashi.eng: *And what pleases you.* And what pleases you and your brethren (to do) with the rest of the silver and the gold, according to the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, you shall do.

rashi.heb:
*ומאניא.* 
וכלים הנתונים לך לעבודתו של הקדוש ברוך הוא שלם לפני הקב"ה בירושלים:
rashi.eng: *And the vessels.* And the vessels that are given to you for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, give in their entirety before the Holy One, blessed be He, in Jerusalem.

notes.241: (tn): Aram “may fall to you to give.”

rashi.heb:
*ושאר חשחות.* 
ושאר צריכות שתצטרך לביתו של הקב"ה לקנות אשר יהיה לך ליתן הדמים תתן מאוצר המלך:
rashi.eng: *And the rest of the necessities.* and the rest of the necessities that you will require for the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, to purchase, for which you will have to give the money; you shall give from the royal treasury.

rashi.heb:
*ומני אנה.* 
וממני אני דריוש המלך יוצא ציווי ורשות לכל הגזברים אשר בעב' הנהר לצד א"י המקבלים מסים שלי מן העובדי כוכבים אשר כל דבר שישאל מכם עזרא הכהן סופר התורה של הקב"ה מהרה יעשה שלא יעכבו את שאלתו עד מאה ככרים של כסף לקנות קרבנות ומאה כורי' חטין למנחות ועד מאה מדות יין לנסכים ומאה (מדות) של שמן לבלול מנחות ומלח לקרבנות כענין שנא' (ויקרא ב׳:י״ג) וכל קרבן מנחתך במלח תמלח:
rashi.eng: *And from me-I.* And from me-I, King Darius-is issued a command and an authorization to all the treasurers who are on the other side of the river of the side of Israel, who receive my taxes from the nations, that anything that Ezra the priest, the scholar of the Law of the Holy One, blessed be He, requests of you, shall be performed quickly. They should not delay his request up to a hundred talents of silver, with which to purchase sacrifices, and a hundred kors of wheat for meal-offerings, and up to a hundred measures of wine for the libations, and a hundred measures of oil to mingle the meal-offerings, and salt for the sacrifices, according to the matter that is stated (Lev. 2:13): “And every meal-offering you shall salt with salt.”

notes.243: (tc): The translation reads מְשַׁח בַּתִּין (m�shakh battin) rather than מְשַׁח בַּתִּין (battin m�shakh) of the MT.

rashi.heb:
*די לא כתב.* 
ומלח שאין כתוב בו מדה יתנו ככל הצורך:
rashi.eng: *which is not written.* And salt, regarding which no measure is written, they shall give according to how much is needed.

notes.245: (tn, Heb): The Aramaic word used here for “wrath” (קְצַף, q�tsaf; cf. קָצַף, qatsaf) is usually used in the Hebrew Bible for God’s anger as opposed to human anger (but contra Eccl 5:17 [MT 5:16]; Esth 1:18; 2 Kgs 3:27). The fact that this word is used in v. 23 may have theological significance, pointing to the possibility of divine judgment if the responsible parties should fail to make available these provisions for the temple.

rashi.heb:
*כל די מן טעם.* 
כל אשר יהיה מרשותו של הקב"ה וציוויו יעשה בזריזות בחותם המלך לביתו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *Whatever is with the authorization.* Whatever is with the authorization of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His command, shall be done with alacrity, with the seal of the king for the House of the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*אדרזדא.* 
חותם בלשון ערבי:
rashi.eng: *with a seal.* Aram. אַדְרַזְדָּא, seal in Arabic.

rashi.heb:
*די למה להוא.* 
אשר למה יהיה קצף על מלכות המלך ובניו ועל כן יתנו הגזברים כל צרכי הבית:
rashi.eng: *for why should there be.* For why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons? Therefore, the treasurers shall provide all the needs of the House.

notes.246: (tn): Aram “we are making known to you.”

rashi.heb:
*ולכום מהודעין.* 
ולכם אנו מודיעים אשר כל הכהנים והלוים המשוררים והשוערים והנתינים שהם חוטבי עצים ושואבי מים למזבח ועובדים בבית זה של הקב"ה לא ישלוט אדם עליהם להשליך עליהם מס וכסף גולגולת אלא יהיו בני חורין מעבודת המלך:
rashi.eng: *And we are making known to you.* And we are making known to you that [over] all the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the gatekeepers, and the Nethinites, who are wood cutters and water drawers for the altar, and those who serve in this House of the Holy One, no man shall be empowered over them to levy upon them any tribute or head tax, but they shall be free from the service of the king.

notes.248: (tc): For the MT reading שָׁפְטִין (shoftim, “judges”) the LXX uses the noun γραμματεῖς (grammatei", “scribes”).

rashi.heb:
*ואנת עזרא כחכמת אלהיך די בידך.* 
ואתה עזרא כפי חכמת אלהיך אשר בידיך יותר מן השופטים והדיינים שהם דנין כל העם שבעבר הנהר לצד ארץ ישראל עם יודעי התורה:
rashi.eng: *And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God, which is in your hand.* and you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God, which is in your hand [and which is] greater than that of the judges and the magistrates who judge all the people beyond the river to the side of Israel, the people knowledgeable in the Torah.

rashi.heb:
*ודי לא ידע.* 
והשופט אשר לא ידע לשפוט תודיע לו המשפט לעשותו:
rashi.eng: *and whoever does not know.* and the judge who does not know how to judge, inform him of the judgment that he should execute it.

notes.249: (tn): On the meaning of this word see HALOT 1820-21 s.v. אָסְפַּרְנָא; E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 14.

rashi.heb:
*וכל די לא להוא עבד.* 
וכל אשר לא יהיה עושה דתו של הקב"ה ודת המלך מהרה יעכב הדין והמשפט:
rashi.eng: *And whoever does not fulfill.* and whoever does not fulfill the law of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the law of the king promptly, viz. that he delays the law and the judgment.

rashi.heb:
*דינה.* 
הדין יעשה ממנו מן המעכב משפט:
rashi.eng: *judgment.* The judgment shall be inflicted upon him, upon the one who obstructs justice.

rashi.heb:
*הן למות.* 
להרג:
rashi.eng: *whether to be executed.* [as translated,] whether to be executed.

rashi.heb:
*הן לשרושי.* 
אם לעקרו מן העולם אותו ואת זרעו ואת משפחתו, לשרושי דישראצינ"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *uprooted.* whether to uproot him from the world, him, his offspring and his family (לִשְּׁרשִׁי is desraziner in Old French, to uproot).

rashi.heb:
*הן לענוש נכסין.* 
אם לענשו בממון:
rashi.eng: *fined.* to be punished with money.

rashi.heb:
*ולאסורין.* 
או לייסרו בייסורין, עד כאן מכתב האגרת אשר נתן דריוש המלך לעזרא הסופר למען ישאהו לירושלים להראותו אל הכהנים והלוים וגזברי המלך למען יחזיקו לקיים המצות ולעבוד ה' בבית המקדש ולשמור התורה כמשפט:
rashi.eng: *or tortured.* or to torture him with tortures. Until here is the writ of the letter that King Darius gave to Ezra the scribe in order that he convey it to Jerusalem to show it to the priests and the Levites and the king’s treasurers, in order that they persist in performing the commandments and worshiping the Lord in the Temple and keeping the Torah properly.

notes.250: (sn): At this point the language of the book reverts from Aramaic (7:12-26) back to Hebrew.

rashi.heb:
*ברוך ה'.* 
כך כתב עזרא בספרו כאשר נתן הודאה להקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *Blessed be the Lord.* Ezra wrote this in his Book when he gave thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*ויועציו.* 
הם שבעה רואי פני המלך הן שבעה יעטוהי של מעלה:
rashi.eng: *and his advisers.* They are his seven advisers mentioned above (verse 14).

rashi.heb:
*כיד ה' אלהי עלי.* 
כאשר היתה עזרתו של הקב"ה עלי וקבצתי מישראל הנשארים בבבל ראשי אבות וגדולים לעלות עמי מבבל:
rashi.eng: *according to the hand of the Lord my God upon me.* as the help of the Holy One, blessed be He, was upon me; and I gathered from the Israelites remaining in Babylon the chiefs of the fathers’ houses and the great men to ascend with me from Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*ואלה ראשי אבותיהם.* 
של עולים:
rashi.eng: *And these are the heads of their fathers’ houses.* of the immigrants.

rashi.heb:
*והתיחשם.* 
את יחוסם אשר היו מתייחשים בהם:
rashi.eng: *and the lineage.* and their lineage to which they attributed their descent.

rashi.heb:
*ארתחשסתא.* 
הוא דריוש:
rashi.eng: *Artaxerxes.* He is Darius.

notes.252: (tc): The MT reads here “from the sons of Shecaniah” with no descendant identified in what follows, contrary to the pattern of the context elsewhere. However, it seems better to understand the first phrase of v. 3 with the end of v. 2; the phrase would then modify the name “Hattush.” This understanding requires emending the reading מִבְּנֵי (mibb�ne, “from the sons of”) in the MT to בֵּן (ben,“[the] son of”). Cf. NAB, TEV, CEV, NLT.

rashi.heb:
*מבני שכניה מבני פרעש.* 
משפחה אחת היא וזכריה הוא ראש המשפחה:
rashi.eng: *Of the sons of Shechaniah, of the sons of Parosh.* That is one family, and Zechariah was the head of the family.

rashi.heb:
*ועמו.* 
ועם יחס שלו היו מתיחסים הזכרים של משפחתו:
rashi.eng: *and with him.* With his lineage, the males of his family traced their lineage.

notes.253: (tc): The MT lacks “of Zattu.” The translation adopted above follows the LXX in including the words.

rashi.heb:
*עבד בן יונתן.* 
כך שמו:
rashi.eng: *Ebed the son of Jonathan.* That was his name.

notes.254: (tc): The MT lacks “Bani.” It is restored on the basis of certain LXX MSS.

notes.255: (tn): Or “those who came later.” The exact meaning of this Hebrew phrase is uncertain. It may refer to the last remaining members of Adonikam’s family who were in Babylon. So, for example, H. G. M. Williamson, Ezra, Nehemiah (WBC), 108; cf. NASB, NIV, NCV. The phrase has also been taken to mean “the younger sons (so NAB), or the ones who “returned at a later date” (so TEV).

rashi.heb:
*אחרונים.* 
שהיו אחרונים ללכת אחרי עזרא:
rashi.eng: *the last ones.* who were the last ones to go after Ezra.

notes.256: (tc): The translation reads with the Qere, the Lucianic Greek recension, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Vulgate וְזַּכּוּר (v�zakkur, “and Zaccur”) rather than the Kethib of the MT, וְזַבוּד (v�zavud, “and Zabbud”).
notes.257: (tn): The MT has “with him” (so NAB). The present translation (“with them”) is based on the reading of many medieval Hebrew MSS, the Lucianic Greek recension, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Vulgate (so also KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*אל הנהר הבא.* 
אל הנהר הנובע:
rashi.eng: *to the flowing river.* Heb. הַבָּא אֶל הַנָהָר, lit. to the coming river.

rashi.heb:
*אל אהוא.* 
אל אותו הנהר:
rashi.eng: *to Ahava.* to that river.

rashi.heb:
*ונחנה שם.* 
והיינו חונים שם:
rashi.eng: *and we encamped there.* and we were camping there.

rashi.heb:
*ואבינה בעם.* 
נתתי לבי להבין בעם אשר נקבצו עמי:
rashi.eng: *and I surveyed the people.* I directed my attention to survey the people who had gathered with me.

notes.260: (tc): The name “Elnathan” occurs twice in this list. Some, assuming an accidental repetition, would include it only once (cf. NAB).

rashi.heb:
*ואשלחה לאליעזר וגו'.* 
ראשים, גדולים:
rashi.eng: *And I sent to Eliezer… the heads.* the great men.

rashi.heb:
*מבינים.* 
חכמים היו:
rashi.eng: *the wise men.* Heb. מְבִינִים, lit. understanding. They were wise men.

notes.261: (tn, Heb): “I placed in their mouth words.”
notes.262: (tc): The translation reads with the LXX and Vulgate וְאֶחָיו (v�’ekhayv, “and his brethren” = “relatives”; so NCV, NLT) rather than the reading אָחִיו (’akhiyv, “his brother”) of the MT.
notes.263: (tn, Heb): “in the place called.” This phrase has not been repeated in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*ואצוה אותם וגו'.* 
שלחתים וצויתים לדבר אל אדו שהוא גדול וחשוב אשר בכספיא:
rashi.eng: *And I commanded them, etc..* I sent them and commanded them to speak to Iddo, who was the greatest and most esteemed in Casiphia.

rashi.heb:
*על אדו.* 
אל אדו:
rashi.eng: *to Iddo.* Heb. עַל אִדוֹ, lit. about Iddo.

rashi.heb:
*ואשימה בפיהם.* 
שמתי בפיהם דברים לדבר בשליחותי אל אדו ואחיו שהם נתונים ומיושבים בכספיא להביא לנו משרתים לעבוד בבית המקדש:
rashi.eng: *and I put… into their mouth.* I put into their mouth words to speak as my emissary to Iddo and his brother, who were placed and settled in Casiphia, to bring us servants to serve in the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*בכספיא.* 
שם מקום בבבל:
rashi.eng: *in Casiphia.* the name of a place in Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*אל אדו אחיו.* 
שם אדם:
rashi.eng: *Ahiv.* the name of a man.

rashi.heb:
*הנתינים.* 
כמו הנתינים ועל כן נכתב בוי"ו:
rashi.eng: *who were settled.* Heb. הַנְתִינִים, like הַנְתוּנִים, those who were settled. Therefore, it is written with a “vav.”

notes.264: (tn, Heb): “and Sherebiah.” The words “this man was” are not in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.
notes.265: (tn): Or “relatives” (so CEV; NRSV “kin”); also in v. 19.

rashi.heb:
*כיד אלהינו.* 
כאשר היתה הצלחתו של הקדוש ברוך הוא עלינו:
rashi.eng: *according to the hand of our God.* just as the success of the Holy One, blessed be He, was upon us.

rashi.heb:
*איש שכל.* 
חכם:
rashi.eng: *a man of intellect.* a wise man.

rashi.heb:
*מבני מחלי וגו'.* 
כולם הללו לוים:
rashi.eng: *of the sons of Mahli….* All these were Levites.

rashi.heb:
*ומן הנתינים.* 
ומן העבדים נתינים שנתן דוד המלך ושרי ישראל עלו עמהם:
rashi.eng: *And of the Nethinites.* And of the slaves, the Nethnites that King David had appointed, and the chefs of Israel ascended with them.

rashi.heb:
*להתענות.* 
לישב בתענית:
rashi.eng: *to fast.* Heb. לְהִתְעַנוֹת to fast.

rashi.heb:
*דרך ישרה.* 
שיוליכני המקום לשלום:
rashi.eng: *a straight way.* that the Omnipresent lead us in peace.

notes.267: (tn): A number of modern translations regard this as a collective singular and translate “from enemies” (also in v. 31).
notes.268: (tn, Heb): “his strength and his anger.” The expression is a hendiadys (one concept expressed through two terms).

rashi.heb:
*כי בושתי.* 
שהרי נתביישתי מן המלך שלא רציתי לשאול לו רכב ופרשים כדי לתיירנו:
rashi.eng: *For I was ashamed.* For I was ashamed of the king, and I did not wish to request of him chariots and horsemen in order to guide us.

rashi.heb:
*כי אמרנו.* 
שהרי כבר אמרנו אל דריוש המלך שהקב"ה מטיב למבקשיו ושופך אפו וחמתו על עוזביו:
rashi.eng: *for we had said.* For we had already said to King Darius that the Holy One, blessed be He, benefits those who seek Him and pours out His wrath and His anger upon those who forsake Him.

rashi.heb:
*ויעתר לנו.* 
וקבל תפלתינו שבאנו לירושלים לשלום:
rashi.eng: *and He accepted our prayer.* for we arrived safely in Jerusalem.

notes.269: (tc): The translation reads וַחֲשַׁבְיָה וְשֵׁרֵבְיָה (v�sherev�yah vakhashavyah, “and Sherebiah and Hashabiah”) rather than the reading חֲשַׁבְיָה לְשֵׁרֵבְיָה (l�sherevyah khashavyah, “to Sherebiah Hashabiah”) of the MT.

rashi.heb:
*ואבדילה.* 
וכאשר הייתי שם על נהר אהוא הבדלתי משרי הכהנים ושקלתי להם הכסף והזהב ליתן באוצרות בית ה':
rashi.eng: *And I separated.* And when I was there by the river Ahava, I separated some of the chiefs of the priests and weighed out the silver and the gold for them to deposit into the treasuries of the House of the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*ההרימו.* 
אשר הרימו הנמצאים בבבל:
rashi.eng: *which… had offered.* which those living in Babylon had offered.

notes.272: (tn): Possibly “100 silver vessels worth [?] talents” or “silver vessels weighing 100 talents.”

rashi.heb:
*וכלי כסף מאה לככרים.* 
ככר בכל כלי:
rashi.eng: *and one hundred silver vessels by talents.* one talent for each vessel.

rashi.heb:
*וכפורי.* 
מזרקים:
rashi.eng: *And… sprinkling bowls.* bowls for sprinkling [the blood of the sacrifices].

rashi.heb:
*לאדרכונים אלף.* 
מין מטבע אלף דרכונים היו בב' כפורי זהב הללו:
rashi.eng: *of one thousand darics.* a type of coin. There were one thousand darics in these twenty sprinkling bowls of gold.

rashi.heb:
*מוצהב.* 
משל נחושת מוצהב (או) מין מטבע של נחושת:
rashi.eng: *golden.* of golden copper (or) a type of copper coin.

rashi.heb:
*טובה.* 
ל' נקבה קורא לנחושת:
rashi.eng: *fine.* Heb. טוֹבָה, the feminine form, modifying copper (נְחֹשֶּׁת).

rashi.heb:
*שנים.* 
שני כלים:
rashi.eng: *two.* two vessels.

rashi.heb:
*חמודות כזהב.* 
הכלים קורא חמודות בל' נקבה:
rashi.eng: *precious as gold.* Heb. חֲמוּדוֹת כַּזָהָב. He calls the vessels חֲמוּדוֹת in the feminine form.

rashi.heb:
*אליהם.* 
לאותן שרי הכהנים:
rashi.eng: *to them.* to these chiefs of the priests.

notes.273: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*הלשכות בית ה'.* 
כדי ליתן בלשכות הבית:
rashi.eng: *the chambers of the House of the Lord.* in order to deposit them in the chambers of the Temple.

notes.275: (tn, Heb): “from the hand of the enemy and the one who lies in wait.” Some modern English versions render the latter phrase as “ambushes” (cf. NASB, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*בשנים עשר לחודש הראשון.* 
בשנים עשר לניסן:
rashi.eng: *on the twelfth of the first month.* on the twelfth of Nissan

rashi.heb:
*ויד אלהינו היתה עלינו.* 
להצליחנו על הדרך אשר הלכנו עליה:
rashi.eng: *the hand of our God was upon us.* to cause us to succeed in the way that we traversed.

notes.277: (tn): The words “everything was verified” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*במספר במשקל לכל.* 
מספר הכלים ומשקלם כאשר קבלוהו כך היה נשקל כולו כאשר פרעוהו:
rashi.eng: *Everything was counted and weighed.* The number of the vessels and their weights was the same when they received them as when they itemized them.

rashi.heb:
*הבאים מהשבי בני הגולה.* 
הללו אשר באו עם עזרא:
rashi.eng: *Those coming from captivity, the people of the exile.* those who came with Ezra.

rashi.heb:
*הקריבו עולות.* 
הכל עולה והוראת שעה היתה:
rashi.eng: *offered up burnt offerings.* all were burnt offerings, and it was a temporary ruling.

rashi.heb:
*ויתנו את דתי המלך.* 
הללו עולי גולה ספרו מצות דריוש המלך לגדולי המלך רואי פניו:
rashi.eng: *And they gave the king’s decrees.* These returnees from exile related King Darius’s mandate to the officers of the king, those who see his face.

rashi.heb:
*ופחוות.* 
כמו ופחות:
rashi.eng: *and the governors.* Heb. וּפַחֲווֹת, like וְפַחוֹת.

rashi.heb:
*עבר הנהר.* 
אותן של צד ארץ ישראל הן בעבר הנהר ליושבי בבל:
rashi.eng: *the land beyond the river.* those on the side of the land of Israel, who are considered as being beyond the river of the inhabitants of Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*ונשאו.* 
שהיו מנשאין ומסייעין:
rashi.eng: *and they exalted.* They were exalting and assisting.

notes.278: (tn, Heb): “the peoples of the lands.” So also in v. 2.

rashi.heb:
*אלה.* 
דברים הללו אשר ספרו דתי המלך:
rashi.eng: *these.* these incidents that related the kings’ decrees.

rashi.heb:
*והשרים.* 
של ישראל:
rashi.eng: *the chiefs.* of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*לאמר.* 
וכן אמרו לי:
rashi.eng: *saying.* And so they said to me.

notes.279: (tn, Heb): “the holy seed,” referring to the Israelites as God’s holy people.

rashi.heb:
*היתה במעל הזה ראשונה.* 
שהם התחילו למעול מעל להתחתן בגויי הארצות:
rashi.eng: *was first in this treachery.* for they commenced to deal treacherously by intermarrying with the peoples of the lands.

rashi.heb:
*משומם.* 
עלוב ושומם כמו (יחזקאל ג׳:ט״ו) שבעת ימים משמים בתוכם:
rashi.eng: *I rent my garment.* out of the great pain due to this treachery. bewildered Heb. מְשּׁוֹמֵם miserable and bewildered, like (Ez. 3:15): “… seven days bewildered among them.”

notes.280: (tn, Heb): “who trembled at the words of the God of Israel.”
notes.281: (tn, Heb): “the exile”; the words “the people” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied in the translation for clarity.

notes.282: (tn): The Hebrew word used here is a hapax legomenon. It refers to the self-abasement that accompanies religious sorrow and fasting.

rashi.heb:
*מתעניתי.* 
שלא אכלתי אותו יום:
rashi.eng: *from my fast.* for I had not eaten on that day.

notes.284: (tc): The MT lacks “and” here, but see the LXX and Vulgate.

rashi.heb:
*נתנו.* 
כמו נתננו דגש הנו"ן תחת חסרון נו"ן אחרת כמו (ד"ה ב' י"ד) כי עליך נשענו כמו נשעננו (בראשית ל״ד:ט״ז) ונתנו את בנותינו כמו ונתננו:
rashi.eng: *we were delivered.* Heb. נִתַּנוּ, like נִתַּנְנוּ. The “dagesh” in the “nun” is instead of another “nun,” like (II Chron. 14:10): “for we rely (תִשְּׁעַנוּ) on You,” like נִשְּׁעַנְנוּ. (Gen. 34:16): “… then we will give (וְנָתַנוּ) our daughters,” like וְנָתַנְנוּ.

rashi.heb:
*כהיום הזה.* 
כמו שנראה היום הזה שכבר גלו עשרת השבטים ועדיין נשארו בבבל הרבה מן הגולים:
rashi.eng: *as of this day.* as appears this day, for the Ten Tribes have already been exiled, and many of the exiles still remain in Babylon.

notes.287: (tn, Heb): “a peg” or “tent peg.” The imagery behind this word is drawn from the experience of nomads who put down pegs as they pitched their tents and made camp after times of travel.
notes.288: (tn, Heb): “to cause our eyes to shine.” The expression is a figure of speech for “to revive.” See DCH 1:160 s.v. אור Hi.7.

rashi.heb:
*ועתה כמעט רגע.* 
לפי שעה:
rashi.eng: *And now, for a short moment.* temporarily.

rashi.heb:
*תחנה.* 
כמו חנינה:
rashi.eng: *favor.* Heb. תְּחִנָה, like חֲנִינָה

rashi.heb:
*ולתת לנו יתד.* 
לקבוע אותנו בארץ ישראל:
rashi.eng: *and to give us a peg.* to establish us in the land of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*יתד.* 
כמו (ישעיהו כ״ב:כ״ג) ותקעתיו יתד במקום נאמן:
rashi.eng: *a peg.* יָתֵד, like (Isa. 22:23): “And I will thrust him like a peg (יָתֵד) in a sure place.”

rashi.heb:
*מחיה מעט.* 
חיים מועטים:
rashi.eng: *a little life.* [as translated,] a little life.

notes.291: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*כי עבדים אנחנו.* 
לדריוש מלך פרס:
rashi.eng: *For we are slaves.* to Darius, king of Persia.

rashi.heb:
*ולא עזבנו.* 
לא עזב אותנו:
rashi.eng: *has not forsaken us.* Heb. לֹא עֲזָבָנוּ, a combination of לֹא עָזַב אוֹתָנוּ.

rashi.heb:
*ויט.* 
לשון מפעל כמו מטה הטה עלינו חסדו:
rashi.eng: *and He has extended.* Heb. וַיַט, an expression of the causative, like מַטֶה. He extended His loving-kindness upon us.

rashi.heb:
*גדר.* 
שהיו גודרין גדר לשמור מצותיו:
rashi.eng: *a fence.* for they had created a fence to keep His commandments.

notes.292: (tn, Heb): “through your servants the prophets, saying.”

rashi.heb:
*נדה.* 
טמאה וגעולה:
rashi.eng: *unclean.* Heb. נִדָה, unclean and repulsive.

notes.294: (tn, Heb): “sons”; cf. KJV, NAB, NIV, NLT “children”; NCV, TEV “descendants.”

rashi.heb:
*והורשתם.* 
את הארץ לבניכם עד עולם:
rashi.eng: *and you shall cause… to inherit.* You shall give the land to your children as an inheritance to eternity.

notes.295: (tn, Heb): “held back downwards from”; KJV “hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve” (NIV, NRSV, NLT all similar).

rashi.heb:
*ואחרי כל הבא עלינו.* 
אחרי כל המעשה הרע אשר הגיע עלינו במעשינו הרעים:
rashi.eng: *And after all that has come upon us.* after all the calamity that has befallen us because of our evil deeds.

rashi.heb:
*חשכת.* 
למטה מעונינו מנעת מעונותינו עד למטה שנפחת עונינו על כפרת גלותינו ויש לנו לפותרו בענין זה מנעת עצמך מלגבות ממנו כל עונינו וגבית ממנו למטה מן העונות ולא פרעת ממנו ככל חטאתינו:
rashi.eng: *You have punished less.* You have held back from our iniquities until below them [i.e., less than them], for our iniquity was lessened by the expiation effected by our exile. We may also interpret it in this manner: You held Yourself back from collecting from us all our iniquity, and You collected from us below [less than] the iniquities, and You requited us according to all our sins.

rashi.heb:
*הנשיב.* 
אם נשוב:
rashi.eng: *If we revert.* Heb. הֲנָשּׁוּב, if we return.

rashi.heb:
*הלא תאנף בנו.* 
תמיה המתקיימת:
rashi.eng: *will You not be wroth with us.* a wonder with an affirmative answer.

notes.296: (tn, Heb): “this”; the referent (the guilt mentioned previously) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*כי אין.* 
כח מעשים טובים בנו לעמוד ולהתקיים לפניך על עבירה זו:
rashi.eng: *for we cannot.* lit. for there is nothing; i.e., we do not have the power of good deeds to stand and exist before You, because of this transgression.

rashi.heb:
*בכה.* 
כמו בכי:
rashi.eng: *weeping.* Heb. בּכֶה, like בֶּכִי.

notes.298: (tc): The translation reads with the Qere, many medieval Hebrew MSS, the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate עֵילָם (’elam, “Elam”) rather than the reading עוֹלָם (’olam, “eternity”) found in the MT.
notes.299: (tn, Heb): “in that we have given a dwelling to.” So also in vv. 14, 17, 18.

rashi.heb:
*ונושב.* 
והושבנום:
rashi.eng: *and we have taken.* And we took them in.

rashi.heb:
*יש מקוה.* 
יש תקוה לישראל על כך שהם יכולים להוציא נשיהם העכו"ם והנולד מהם ולהוציא כל הבנים הנולדים מן הנשים העכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *there is hope.* There is hope for Israel concerning this, for they can cast out their foreign wives and their offspring and cast out all the children born from these foreign wives.

notes.303: (tn): The MT vocalizes this word as a plural, which could be understood as a reference to God. But the context seems to suggest that a human lord is intended. The apparatus of BHS suggests repointing the word as a singular (“my lord”), but this is unnecessary. The plural (“my lords”) can be understood in an honorific sense even when a human being is in view. Most English versions regard this as a reference to Ezra, so the present translation supplies “your” before “counsel” to make this clear.
notes.304: (tn, Heb): “who tremble at”; NAB, NIV “who fear.”

rashi.heb:
*בעצת אד'.* 
בעצתו וברצונו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *by the counsel of the Lord.* by the counsel and the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*וחרדים במצות אלהינו.* 
ויראי שמים יוציאם:
rashi.eng: *and those who hasten to [perform] the commandment of our God.* and the God-fearers, they shall cast them out.

rashi.heb:
*וכתורה יעשה.* 
העושה המעשה הזה אשר יוציא אשתו ובניו העובדי כוכבים:
rashi.eng: *and according to the Law it shall be done.* he who performs this act, who will cast out his gentile wife and children.

rashi.heb:
*ואנחנו עמך.* 
להיות מסכימים עמך:
rashi.eng: *and we are with you.* to agree with you.

notes.305: (tn, Heb): “to do according to this plan.”

notes.306: (tc): The translation reads וַיָּלֶן (vayyalen, “and he stayed”) rather than the reading וַיֵּלֶךְ (vayyelekh, “and he went”) of the MT. Cf. the LXX.

notes.309: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*קול.* 
כרוז:
rashi.eng: *a proclamation.* Heb. קוֹל, lit. a voice, an announcement.

rashi.heb:
*לשלשת הימים.* 
לסוף שלשת הימים:
rashi.eng: *by three days.* at the end of three days.

rashi.heb:
*חדש התשיעי.* 
הוא חדש כסליו:
rashi.eng: *the ninth month.* That is the month of Kislev.

rashi.heb:
*מרעידים על הדבר.* 
מתייראים על הדבר ומתייראים היו ממכשול של עבירה זאת:
rashi.eng: *quaking over the matter.* They were afraid over the matter. They were afraid of the stumbling block of this transgression.

rashi.heb:
*ומהגשמים.* 
ומן הגשמים היורדים עליהם שם היו רעודים ועלובים:
rashi.eng: *and because of the rains.* And because of the rains that were falling upon them there, they were shivering and miserable.

rashi.heb:
*תודה.* 
וידוי:
rashi.eng: *confess.* Heb. תּוֹדָה, [which, in this case, means] וִדּוּי, confession.

notes.311: (tn, Heb): “thus according to your word [singular = Qere] concerning us, to do.”

rashi.heb:
*והעת גשמים.* 
שהגשמי' יורדי' עלינו:
rashi.eng: *and it is the rainy season.* for the rains are falling upon us.

rashi.heb:
*והמלאכה.* 
והרחקת עבירה זו אין אתה יכול לתקן כל כך במהירות:
rashi.eng: *and the work.* And this separation from sin cannot be executed so quickly.

rashi.heb:
*לכל הקהל.* 
עם כל הקהל:
rashi.eng: *with the entire congregation.* Heb. לְכָל הַקָהָל

rashi.heb:
*ההושיב.* 
אשר הושיב:
rashi.eng: *who took in.* Heb. הַהשִּׁיב equivalent to אֲשֶּׁר הוֹשִּׁיב.

rashi.heb:
*עד להשיב.* 
עד אשר ישוב חרונו של הקב"ה מעלינו:
rashi.eng: *until we avert.* until the burning anger of the Holy One, blessed be He, returns from upon us.

rashi.heb:
*עמדו על זאת.* 
לקנתר על דבר זה:
rashi.eng: *stood up against this.* to argue concerning this matter.

rashi.heb:
*עזרום.* 
החזיקו ידיהם:
rashi.eng: *supported them.* strengthened their hands.

notes.315: (tc): The translation reads the Hiphil singular וַיַּבְדֵּל לוֹ (vayyavdel lo, “separated for himself”) rather than the Niphal plural וַיִּבָּדְלוּ (vayyibbad�lu, “were separated”) of the MT.
notes.316: (tn, Heb): “the heads of the fathers, to the house of their fathers, and all of them by name.”

rashi.heb:
*לדריוש.* 
כמו לדרוש:
rashi.eng: *to investigate.* Heb. לְדַרְיוֹשּׁ, like לִדְרוֹשּׁ.

rashi.heb:
*ויכלו בכל.* 
והשלימו את תיקון המעשה מן האנשים אשר הושיבו נשים של עובדי כוכבים כי הוציאם:
rashi.eng: *And they completed everything.* And they completed the rectification of the matter of the men who had brought in heathen wives, for they cast them out.
*of the first month.* until the first day of Nissan.

rashi.heb:
*ידם.* 
עצתם כמו הנה יד יואב אתך בכל זאת (שמואל ב י״ד:י״ט):
rashi.eng: *And they advised them.* Heb. וַיִתְּנוּ יָדָם, lit. and they gave their hand, their advice, like (II Sam. 14:19): “Behold Joab’s advice (יַד יוֹאָב) is with you in all this (sic).”

rashi.heb:
*על אשמתם.* 
הוראת שעה היתה:
rashi.eng: *for their guilt.* This was a temporary ruling.

rashi.heb:
*ומבני אמר.* 
כל אלו כהנים עד ומן הלוים וגומר:
rashi.eng: *And of the sons of Immer.* All these are priests until (verse 23): “And of the Levites, etc.”

notes.319: (tc): The translation reads with many medieval Hebrew MSS and ancient versions וּמִבְּנֵי (umibb�ne, “and from the sons of”) rather than the reading ubene (“and the sons of”) found in the MT.

notes.320: (tn): The name “Bani” appears in both v. 29 and v. 34. One of these names has probably undergone alteration in the transmission process, but it is not clear exactly where the problem lies or how it should be corrected.

notes.321: (tc): The translation reads וּמִבְּנֵי בִנּוּי (umibb�ney vinnuy, “and from the sons of Binnui”) rather than the reading וּבָנִי וּבִנּוּי (uvani uvinnuy, “and Bani and Binnui”) of the MT.

notes.322: (tc): The final statement in v. 44 is difficult in terms of both its syntax and its meaning. The present translation attempts to make sense of the MT. But the passage may have undergone corruption in the transmission process. One proposal is that the text should be emended to read “and they sent these wives and children away” (cf. NAB, NRSV, TEV, CEV).

rashi.heb:
*ויש מהם נשים וישימו בנים.* 
מקצתן שהיו להם נשים של עובדי כוכבים שנולדו להם מהם בנים והכל הוציאו הנשים והבנים:
rashi.eng: *and some of them had wives by whom they had children.* And some of them had heathen wives by whom they had children. They cast out all of them, both the wives and the children.
